description: SET condition-name TO FALSE (ISO 14.9.39 Format 4 - the FALSE arm). 14.9.39.4 GR7 places 'the literal in the FALSE phrase of the VALUE clause associated with condition-name-1' in the conditional variable, and 14.9.39.3 SR7 requires that phrase to be there (COBOL2049). A COBOL-2002 introduction, paired with its VALUE-clause half (value-false-phrase-2002, VCR row 7.32). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 SET sets a condition-name only to TRUE (§1985:VI.6.23.2 Format 4: `SET {condition-name-1} … TO TRUE`; §1985:VI.6.23.4 GR7: 'The literal in the VALUE clause associated with condition-name-1 is placed in the conditional variable'); §2002:14.8.35.2 SR7 reads 'If the FALSE phrase is specified, the FALSE phrase shall be specified in the VALUE clause of the data description entry for condition-name-1' and §2002:14.8.35.3 GR6 'If the FALSE phrase is specified, the literal in the FALSE phrase of the VALUE clause associated with condition-name-1 is placed in the conditional variable', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 144: 'This value is moved to the associated conditional variable when the SET TO FALSE statement is executed for the associated condition-name.' §2014:14.9.35.2 SR7 and §2014:14.9.35.3 GR7 carry it, so 2014 = 2023. Recognition-fired by VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitSetBooleanStatement on the FALSE_ token, so the gate survives the SR7 refusal. The row's source necessarily writes the VALUE phrase too, so below 2002 BOTH gates fire - the matrix asserts presence of the code, not its multiplicity. kb/Work PB555.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMSETFA.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 CV PIC 9 VALUE 1.
   88 CN VALUE 1 WHEN SET TO FALSE IS 7.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    SET CN TO FALSE.
    DISPLAY CV.
    STOP RUN.
